$comment: An entry is legitimate ONLY when the advisory has no published fix — every released version
of the package falls inside the vulnerable range, so no bump, resolution or lockfile edit can
clear it. Everything else is fixed by upgrading, not waived.
A waiver suppresses an advisory only while the package, the GHSA id and the exact vulnerable
range the registry reports all match, and only until `expires`; after that the gate goes red
again on its own. `expires` may not be more than 90 days out, and a waiver that stops matching
anything is reported as stale so it gets removed.

waivers.reason: No fixed release exists: 2.0.2 is the newest published version and the advisory's first_patched_version is null, so the vulnerable range covers the whole package history. Reachable only from apps/docs through @docusaurus/mdx-loader, which measures repo-authored images while building the documentation site — no runtime package or app depends on it and the inputs are not attacker-controlled. Tracked by #5144; drop this waiver the moment image-size ships a fix.
Same package, same absence of a fixed release, same docs-build-only reach as GHSA-w3rx-r6r6-pgpr above (JXL and HEIF parsers rather than ICNS). Tracked by #5144.
